name: Kuwait Finance House (Bahrain)
legal_name: Kuwait Finance House B.S.C. (c) (formerly Ahli United Bank B.S.C. (c); renamed 10 Jul 2025)
founded: Incorporated in Bahrain on 12 Jul 2000 as Ahli United Bank B.S.C.; acquired by KFH in 2022; Islamic retail bank licence from 10 Dec 2023; renamed Kuwait Finance House B.S.C. (c) on 10 Jul 2025
regulators: CBI (Commercial Islamic Bank of Iraq subsidiary)
ownership_summary: 100% owned subsidiary of Kuwait Finance House K.S.C.P. (Boursa Kuwait and Bahrain Bourse listed) since KFH acquired Ahli United Bank in 2022. A closed (unlisted) Bahraini joint-stock company (H1 2026 statements, note 1).
government_link: Indirect. Parent KFH's largest holders are Kuwaiti state entities (KIA 15.67%, PIFSS 9.09%, Public Authority for Minors Affairs 6.82% at 31 Dec 2025; see kw-kfh).
group_structure: KFH Bahrain is both a CBB-licensed Islamic retail bank and an intermediate holding company. It owns Kuwait Finance House PLC (UK, 100%), Kuwait Finance House Bank - Egypt (95.7%) and Commercial Islamic Bank of Iraq (85.3%), has a DIFC branch, and holds associates in Bahrain and Libya (United Bank for Commerce & Investment). Its sale of the Ahli Bank Oman stake was completed in 2025. DOUBLE COUNTING: all KFH Bahrain figures here are consolidated 'KFH Bahrain Group' figures (incl. UK, Egypt, Iraq), and they are fully consolidated into KFH group (kw-kfh) totals. Never add bh-kfhbahrain to kw-kfh. Figures are reported in USD (functional currency) under AAOIFI standards. Customer deposits include quasi-equity (unrestricted investment accounts). Bahrain-only standalone figures are not used here.

footprint: At 31 Dec 2025: 78 branches (Bahrain 21, Egypt 45, Iraq 10, UK 1, DIFC 1), associates in Bahrain and Libya, and over 2,900 employees. The annual report overview says 87 branches.
customer_segments: Retail (mass; MyHassad savings), Premium Banking (USD 200k+), Private Banking & Wealth Management (HNW; some products for accredited investors only), business banking/SME, corporate and institutional, treasury clients.
business_lines: Four reporting segments: Retail banking; Corporate banking; Treasury and investments (the largest by operating income, USD 266.3m in H1 2026); and Private banking (USD 25.4m). Products include Shariah-compliant accounts and investment deposits, home, auto and personal financing, cards, trade finance, structured, project and syndicated finance, FX and hedging, a gold account, and KFH Trader online trading. Private banking covers mutual funds, sukuk and fixed income, structured products, dual currency deposits, real estate and PE, DPM and trusts.

capabilities.wealth_summary: KFH Bahrain (the former Ahli United Bank B.S.C.) runs a Private Banking & Wealth Management division under Deputy Group CEO Talal Kaiksow, serving clients from Bahrain and a DIFC branch, with group subsidiaries in the UK, Egypt and Iraq. Its private banking shelf is open-architecture and partner-led: Allfunds for mutual funds (Azimut, BlackRock, Fidelity, PIMCO, Schroders and others; minimum USD 10,000; 1-3% arrangement fee), TFS for Shariah-compliant structured products, Azimut for fixed-income discretionary portfolios, MubasherTrade for equity trading, LaSalle/Nuveen/JLL for real estate, and IQ-EQ for trusts. In 2025 it launched a GCC Discretionary Portfolio Management offering and selected structured products, and prepared Advisory and DPM services for a 2026 launch. Its 2026 plan is to scale Advisory/DPM and expand alternatives and private markets through KFH subsidiaries. It hosts the KFH Group 'Advent Investment Management platform' (parent AR 2025). Below private banking sits Premium Banking (USD 200,000 minimum relationship balance), and the KFH Trader online platform offers self-directed global trading. All operations have been Shariah-compliant since 10 Dec 2023 in Bahrain.

segments.name: KFH Private Banking & Wealth Management
segments.eligibility: Not published. Some products are for accredited investors only (S8), and mutual fund access is subject to the bank's qualification criteria (S9).

private_banking.detail: PBWM division (Deputy Group CEO Talal Kaiksow) is a separate reporting segment: H1 2026 operating income USD 25.4m, with segment liabilities and quasi-equity of USD 2.19bn. Services include RM coverage, banking solutions, financing, fixed income, mutual funds, dual currency deposits, structured products, real estate and private equity, and the KFH Trader platform. 'Private Online Banking DIFC Branch' is offered. Awards listed in AR 2025 include MEED 'Best Private Bank - Bahrain'. It works with group entities for a 'seamless, multi-jurisdictional client experience'. Euromoney (Jun 2026) describes KFH's PBWM, including Bahrain, as consolidated into one group-wide PBWM group in 2025.

asset_management.detail: Note 1 describes the group as engaged in 'banking business, global fund management and private banking services'. Off-balance-sheet assets under management were USD 1.70bn at 30 Jun 2026. Real estate fund management and private equity are offered to private clients. No separate asset management subsidiary is named in the documents checked.

brokerage.detail: KFH Trader is an online trading platform with web and app access, real-time quotes, global markets and portfolio evaluation. Equity trading is through partner MubasherTrade ('online trading access to all major Arab and International stock exchanges'). Fixed income is available via primary and secondary markets, with custody and financing against pledged securities.

digital_investing.detail: Self-directed trading via the KFH Trader app. The mobile banking app offers digital physical-gold buy/sell with delivery (launched 2025, described as a first in Bahrain). Mobile app ratings reached 4.8 (iOS) and 4.9 (Android), and monthly active digital customers grew over 40% in 2025. No in-app funds or portfolio product found.

advisory.detail: RM-led investment advice ('advice, trading and execution'). A formal Advisory service model (policies, committees, controls) was built in 2025 for launch and scaling in 2026.

discretionary.detail: 'GCC Discretionary Portfolio Management offering' launched in 2025. A broader DPM service was prepared for 2026. Azimut is the partner for fixed-income discretionary portfolios, with built-in financing.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or digital model portfolios on the KFH Bahrain site or in AR 2025.

funds_platform.detail: Allfunds provides access to Shariah-compliant funds from Amundi, Azimut, BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs, Invesco, MFS, PineBridge, Schroders, Nomura and others. The fund page also lists Barings, BNY Mellon, Janus Henderson, PIMCO and Russell. Minimum subscription USD/GBP/EUR 10,000; arrangement fee 1.0-3.0%. The fund range was expanded across geographies in 2025.

structured_products.detail: Structured deposits and investments (full or partial principal protection; underlyings include equities, indices, funds, FX and profit rates), sourced via TFS Structured Products (Tradition Group) with access to major issuers. New structured products were launched in 2025.

private_markets.detail: Real estate fund management and private equity for private clients ('best-in-class managers'); real estate partners LaSalle, Nuveen (UK/US real estate) and JLL. The 2026 plan is to expand alternative and private market offerings through KFH subsidiaries.

islamic_wealth.detail: Islamic retail bank licence (CBB). Conversion to Shariah-compliant operations took effect on 10 Dec 2023 in Bahrain, 22 Aug 2024 in the UK, 1 Sep 2024 in Egypt and 1 Jan 2025 in Iraq. Wealth shelf: Shariah-compliant funds, sukuk, structured products and DPM.

opportunities: Explicit 2026 plan to 'scale Advisory and Discretionary Portfolio Management services' and 'further enhanc[e] mutual fund and discretionary portfolio platforms' (S5, PDF p.36).
Wealth is delivered through partners (Allfunds, TFS, Azimut, MubasherTrade), so third-party product and technology is the norm (S8).
No digital wealth or model-portfolio product found: investing in the app is limited to self-directed KFH Trader and gold, while the retail app's monthly active users grew over 40% in 2025 (S5, S15).
New wealth products across the KFHB Group (incl. UK, Egypt, Iraq) go through the Group New Product Committee, chaired by DGCEO PBWM Talal Kaiksow (S5).
Premium Banking (USD 200k minimum) is an affluent tier that is served by RMs only, with no digital investment proposition found (S14).
barriers: Islamic-only (CBB Islamic retail licence): every product needs Shari'a Supervisory Board approval (S4).

100% owned by KFH Kuwait. Group PBWM (Liddle, see kw-kfh) and KFH Capital set group-wide wealth direction, and the Advent platform is already hosted in Bahrain, so vendor choices may be made at group level (inference; not documented) (S19).
Small PB segment by profit: H1 2026 private banking profit before tax was USD 3.6m on USD 25.4m operating income (S3).
